title: I Let the Startup Unlimited-PTO Policy Survive Three Approvers

parts.text: I requested Thursday off in June because unlimited PTO was in the offer letter. My manager, Vic, denied it in the app: bad time. I was twenty-nine, engineer, holding a dentist appointment card. I asked what a good time was. Vic said we would know. I forwarded the offer letter. He said letters are culture, not calendar. Then he posted in standup that people who take time are not owners.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He denied the dentist and defined owners as people who never leave.

social.video_title: Unlimited PTO died in the app as bad time — Part 1/3
social.description: Offer letter, dentist card, standup sermon. Would you have gone to the dentist anyway?

parts.text: I went to HR, approver two. They said Vic had discretion. I asked for the written rubric of discretion. There was a slide that said we trust managers. I asked who trusts dentists. They did not laugh. I booked the cleaning anyway on a Friday Vic was at a conference. The app still said denied. Security badges still opened. I cleaned my teeth. Vic returned and put a note in my review: reliability concerns. I screenshotted the note next to the offer letter's unlimited.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: My review now punishes a cleaning the offer letter allowed.

social.video_title: HR trusted Vic; my badge trusted the dentist — Part 2/3
social.description: No rubric, a conference Friday, a review note. Would you have skipped the cleaning?

parts.text: Approver three was the board observer copied on all reviews that used the word reliability. I sent the packet. Unlimited became a real form with a 48-hour default approve if silent. Vic's sermon vanished from standup lore. My review note was struck. I still work there, which surprises me. Teeth are reliable. Culture that cannot survive a cleaning is a demo. I take Thursdays when I need them. The app says approved because silence is now a yes, which is what unlimited always meant if you read it like a human.

social.video_title: Silence became a yes and the sermon left standup — Part 3/3
social.description: Form, struck note, Thursday. Was ownership a cavity?
